content:
RAFAEL MORETTI-KLEIN
Backend Engineer | Python, Go & Platform Services
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend and platform engineer with extensive experience designing and building production services in Go and Python. Work includes high-throughput entitlement services, a large-scale monolith-to-services migration, and reliability improvements to a playback API. Experienced with FastAPI, gRPC, Kubernetes, GKE, Terraform, observability tooling, and automated testing. Seeking a hands-on individual-contributor role focused on backend engineering.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Python, Go; C++ (project use)
Backend and APIs: FastAPI, gRPC, backend services, playback API
Data stores and analytics: Cassandra, Redis, BigQuery
Cloud and infrastructure: Google Cloud Platform (GKE), Kubernetes, Terraform; AWS EC2 and S3 (limited exposure)
Observability: OpenTelemetry, Prometheus
Testing: pytest, tox
Other: Looker Studio

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Streamhaus GmbH
Director of Engineering | 2019–2026
- Led the platform organisation of 45 engineers.
- Led the technical side of the playback API.
- Contributed to a strangler-fig migration from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python 3 and Go services on GKE.
- Established a service template using FastAPI or Go, with OpenTelemetry tracing, Prometheus metrics, and Terraform modules.
- Helped improve playback API availability from 99.5% to 99.95%.
- Built an internal cloud-cost dashboard using BigQuery billing export, Python scripts, and Looker Studio, with service-level ownership visibility.
- Supported rightsizing and committed-use discounts that saved EUR 4.2 million per year (31%).

Principal Engineer | 2015–2019
- Designed and wrote most of the Go entitlement service, determining what a user could play based on subscriptions, regions, and devices.
- Built the service using gRPC, Cassandra, and local in-memory caching; it handled peak traffic of 120,000 requests per second with p99 latency under 15 ms.
- Served as technical lead for the playback API.

SELECTED PROJECTS
Open-source Python retry library | Maintainer, 2012–2018
- Maintained a Python retry library that reached approximately 1,500 GitHub stars; handed over maintenance in 2018.
- Used pytest and tox.

Patent: Adaptive GPS sampling in vehicle fleets | Co-inventor, Nordfels, 2013
- Co-inventor on a granted German patent for adapting GPS sampling to driving context to reduce data volume.
- Project technologies: C++, statistics.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, professional, technically credible CV with strong quantified achievements: 120,000 requests per second, p99 latency below 15 ms, approximately 60 services, 99.5% to 99.95% availability, and EUR 4.2 million annual savings. The structure is concise and easy to scan. The main content weaknesses are that the two Streamhaus roles are not given separate dates, the recent Director role may obscure the candidate’s hands-on engineering background, and the CV does not clearly distinguish earlier production-service development from the more recent internal-tools and cost-programme work. The document also omits several job-relevant areas that are not supported by the candidate material, including PostgreSQL, relational database work, Docker, CI/CD, Kafka, and logistics-domain experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The single-column section structure, conventional headings, plain text bullets, standard date format, and keyword-rich skills section should parse well in most ATSs. AI screening probability is moderate to good because the CV clearly contains Python, Go, FastAPI, Kubernetes, GKE, Terraform, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, pytest, cloud deployment, APIs, and reliability metrics. Screening performance is reduced because the job’s exact terms REST APIs, Docker, PostgreSQL, schema migrations, query tuning, CI/CD, GitHub Actions, and Kafka are not supported by the candidate material and therefore cannot truthfully be added. The AWS entry is appropriately qualified as limited exposure, which protects credibility but also means the CV will not appear to meet the employer’s AWS preference strongly.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with backend services, Python and Go, FastAPI, cloud deployment, Kubernetes, Terraform, observability, automated testing, high-throughput APIs, reliability engineering, and architecture work. The entitlement service and playback API are especially relevant to the role’s performance and service-ownership expectations. The candidate’s stated preference to return to a hands-on individual-contributor role is reflected appropriately in the summary. The main alignment gaps are solid relational database experience with PostgreSQL, query tuning and schema migrations; Docker; CI/CD; REST API design and consumption as an explicitly documented capability; Kafka or another event-streaming platform; logistics, transport, supply-chain, or EDI experience; and Dutch or French. AWS experience is only limited, while the job uses AWS/EKS. The CV also does not provide evidence about on-call participation, incident response, blameless post-mortems, design notes, or spoken English, although the candidate’s written English and ability to discuss technical trade-offs are evident from the supplied material.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL:
1. In the Professional Experience section, change the Streamhaus dates to reflect the documented departure in August 2026: use “Director of Engineering | 2019–Aug 2026” and “Principal Engineer | 2015–2019” rather than the less precise “2019–2026.”
2. In the Streamhaus experience section, separate the two positions visually with the company shown once and each title, date range, and bullet group clearly associated with that role. This will prevent ATS and recruiter confusion about which achievements belong to the Principal Engineer period versus the Director period.
3. In the Professional Summary, revise the wording so it accurately balances substantial earlier production-service engineering with the more recent leadership and internal-tools work. For example: “Backend and platform engineer with production-service experience in Go and Python, including a high-throughput entitlement service, a migration from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python 3 and Go services, and reliability improvements to a playback API. More recently led a 45-engineer platform organisation and built internal cloud-cost tooling. Now targeting a hands-on individual-contributor backend role.”
4. In the Technical Skills section, retain “AWS EC2 and S3 (limited exposure)” exactly as a qualified skill and do not present AWS as a primary cloud platform. The experience bullets should likewise continue to identify GKE/GCP as the actual cloud deployment environment, avoiding any implication of AWS production depth.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
5. In the Principal Engineer section, make the API and performance evidence more directly searchable without adding unsupported claims. For example, revise “Built the service using gRPC, Cassandra, and local in-memory caching” to “Built a production Go backend service using gRPC, Cassandra, and local in-memory caching; handled peak traffic of 120,000 requests per second with p99 latency under 15 ms.”
6. In the Director of Engineering section, clarify the reliability impact by revising “Helped improve playback API availability from 99.5% to 99.95%” to “Helped improve playback API availability from 99.5% to 99.95% through platform and reliability improvements.”
7. In the Technical Skills section, change “Backend and APIs: FastAPI, gRPC, backend services, playback API” to “Backend and API technologies: FastAPI, gRPC, Python and Go services, playback API.” This uses more specific searchable terminology already supported by the CV while avoiding an unsupported REST claim.
8. Add a short “Selected Engineering Impact” subsection only if space permits, placing the entitlement-service throughput, playback-availability improvement, migration scale, and EUR 4.2 million savings near the top of the CV. Keep the detailed evidence in Experience so the document remains ATS-friendly and does not become repetitive.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, professional, and well structured. It presents strong quantified backend and platform outcomes, including 120,000 requests per second, p99 latency under 15 ms, 99.95% availability, approximately 60 services, and EUR 4.2 million in annual savings. The summary appropriately explains the transition from engineering leadership back to a hands-on individual-contributor role. The main content weakness is that the Director of Engineering section gives limited evidence of recent hands-on coding, while several important capabilities are stated only indirectly. Contact placeholders also make the document incomplete for submission.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The single-column section structure, conventional headings, plain text bullets, and standard technology names are ATS-friendly. The CV includes strong matches for Python, Go, FastAPI, Kubernetes, Terraform, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, pytest, tox, GKE, and cloud services. AI/ATS screening probability is moderate to high for backend, platform, Python/Go, Kubernetes, infrastructure-as-code, observability, and reliability searches. critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document is a strong match for backend service engineering in Go/Python, FastAPI, cloud deployment, Kubernetes, Terraform, observability, automated testing, high-scale API reliability, and technical leadership. It also aligns with the company's emphasis on production ownership and sustainable reliability through the playback API availability improvement and service-template work. The candidate has genuine gaps against the stated must-haves: no PostgreSQL or other relational-database experience with query tuning and schema migrations is documented, Docker is not documented, AWS exposure is limited rather than deployment experience, and CI/CD is not documented. REST API design/consumption, Kafka or another event-streaming platform, logistics/transport/EDI knowledge, and Dutch/French are also not evidenced in the supplied material. These are capability gaps or unsupported areas, not defects that should be invented or overstated in the CV.
critique.improvement_instructions:

1. In the contact-information line beneath the name, replace “[EMAIL]” and “[PHONE]” with the candidate’s actual email address and phone number. Keep the LinkedIn URL as a complete clickable URL if available; do not submit the CV with placeholders.
2. In the Professional Summary section, make the hands-on IC positioning more explicit without overstating recent coding activity. For example, change the final sentence to: “After leading a 45-engineer platform organisation, now targeting a hands-on senior/staff individual-contributor backend role focused on Python, Go, service reliability, and platform engineering.” This preserves the documented target while making the role transition easier for an IC recruiter to understand.
3. In the Professional Experience section under “Director of Engineering | 2019–Aug 2026,” distinguish organisational leadership from documented technical contributions by revising the first two bullets to: “Led a 45-engineer platform organisation while remaining involved in platform architecture and reliability.” and “Led the technical side of the playback API, including platform and reliability improvements that increased availability from 99.5% to 99.95%.” Do not imply that the candidate wrote production code throughout the Director period, because the notes state that coding was limited in the last two years.
4. In the Technical Skills section, keep “AWS EC2 and S3 (limited exposure)” explicitly qualified, as it is now. Do not change it to “AWS” or “AWS deployment,” and do not add Docker, PostgreSQL, relational databases, REST, CI/CD, Kafka, Grafana, or message queues because those capabilities are not supported by the supplied candidate information.

MINOR
5. In the Professional Experience section under “Principal Engineer | 2015–2019,” revise “Built a production Go backend service using gRPC, Cassandra, and local in-memory caching” to “Designed and built a production Go backend service using gRPC, Cassandra, and local in-memory caching.” This more directly matches the job’s emphasis on designing and building backend services while remaining fully supported by the candidate material.
6. In the Technical Skills section, consider changing “Backend and API technologies: FastAPI, gRPC, Python and Go services, playback API” to “Backend and API technologies: FastAPI, gRPC, Python services, Go services, playback API.” The revised parallel wording is easier for ATS parsing and human scanning without claiming unsupported REST experience.
7. In the Open-source project entry, change “Used pytest and tox” to “Tested with pytest and tox.” This makes the testing evidence more direct and searchable while preserving the documented facts.
critique.critical_issues: The CV contains submission-blocking contact placeholders: “[EMAIL]” and “[PHONE]”. Replace them with the candidate’s actual contact details before use. No unsupported skills, tools, certifications, or experiences were detected in the CV when cross-referenced with the supplied candidate information.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, concise, professional, and strongly evidence-based. It presents credible scale and impact through metrics such as 120,000 requests per second, p99 latency under 15 ms, availability improvement from 99.5% to 99.95%, and EUR 4.2 million in annual savings. The summary also clearly explains the transition from engineering leadership back to a senior/staff individual-contributor role. The main content weakness is a duplicated playback-API availability bullet under the Director role. The document also gives limited detail about day-to-day implementation work in the most recent role, which may make the candidate appear more managerial than hands-on despite the stated target.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses conventional section headings, readable chronology, plain text bullets, and strong searchable terms including Python, Go, FastAPI, gRPC, Kubernetes, GKE, Terraform, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, pytest, tox, Cassandra, Redis, and BigQuery. It should parse well in most ATS and has a good AI-screening probability, approximately 80%, for roles emphasizing Python/Go, Kubernetes, Terraform, observability, and backend reliability. Screening probability is reduced for this particular advert because the CV does not explicitly show PostgreSQL, relational database work, query tuning, schema migrations, Docker, REST APIs, CI/CD, GitHub Actions, Kafka, or AWS deployment beyond limited EC2/S3 exposure. These are candidate-experience gaps or unsupported areas rather than terms that should be added without evidence. The skills section is generally clear, although listing 'playback API' as a technology is less ATS-useful than describing the relevant API work in the experience bullets.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns strongly with the comparable-language backend requirement: it shows multiple years of professional Go experience and substantial Python-service exposure, including a migration from Python 2 to approximately 60 Python 3 and Go services. It also aligns very well with the nice-to-have Kubernetes, Terraform, and observability requirements. Reliability, production scale, platform ownership, and technical leadership are especially relevant to the tracking-platform environment. The candidate's material does not establish relational database experience, PostgreSQL, query tuning, schema migrations, Docker, REST API design/consumption, CI/CD, Kafka or another event-streaming platform, logistics/EDI expertise, or Dutch/French language skills. AWS experience is limited to EC2/S3, while the deeper cloud experience is on GCP. These are genuine alignment gaps and should not be presented as skills the CV can claim. The CV does demonstrate strong written technical communication through its clear English presentation and quantified explanations of engineering trade-offs, though spoken-English ability is not directly evidenced.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL:
1. In the Professional Experience section under Streamhaus GmbH, Director of Engineering, remove the duplicated playback-API bullet. Keep the stronger version: "Led the technical side of the playback API, including platform and reliability improvements that increased availability from 99.5% to 99.95%." Delete the later bullet beginning "Helped improve playback API availability..." so the section does not repeat the same achievement.

2. In the Director of Engineering role, make the hands-on individual-contributor relevance more visible by ordering the technical delivery bullets before the organisation-leadership bullet. Place the playback API, monolith migration, service-template, and cost-dashboard bullets first, then the 45-engineer leadership bullet. This will better support the stated target of a senior/staff backend role without changing the facts.

MINOR:
3. In the Technical Skills section, change the heading "Backend and API technologies" to "Backend, API and Services" and retain the supported terms "FastAPI, gRPC, Python services, Go services, playback API." This makes the service/API focus easier for ATS and human reviewers to identify without claiming unsupported REST experience.

4. In the Professional Summary, replace "After leading a 45-engineer platform organisation" with "After leading a 45-engineer platform organisation while remaining involved in platform architecture and reliability". This uses an existing fact from the Director role and more directly connects the leadership experience to the technical requirements of the target position.

5. In the Professional Experience section, revise the service-template bullet to foreground the supported deployment and operations context: "Established a service template for FastAPI and Go services on GKE, with OpenTelemetry tracing, Prometheus metrics, and Terraform modules." This is a clearer, more ATS-readable presentation of information already supported by the candidate material; do not add Docker, AWS, CI/CD, REST, PostgreSQL, or Kafka unless independently verified.
